_comment: First-load JS per route, gzipped, in kilobytes — what a modern browser actually downloads. Legacy noModule polyfills are excluded. Raising a number here is a deliberate, reviewable act; see docs/REBUILD-PLAN.md M0.
_baselineNote: Measured framework floor: React 19 + Next 16 App Router shared runtime, on an empty page. Every route pays this. The default below leaves ~24 kB for route-specific code before CI complains.
_raisedNote: 155 → 158 when the production hygiene batch landed. 158 → 161 for the app menu (M20/M21). Measured before and after on the same tree: every route rose by 2.4 kB and no route rose by more, so this is the shell floor moving rather than one page getting fat. What the 2.4 kB buys, on every route: the menu button, the profile button and its session plumbing, the drawer with its focus trap and scroll lock, the admin gate, the share sheet and the two session forms. The plan budgeted 3 kB for this and specified the fallback if it went over — drop the drawer, make the button a plain link to /menu — so the number was a decision point, not a discovery. The menu's fifty links are not in this figure: they are server-rendered HTML.
_routesNote: Per-route ceilings, for a route that carries something the others do not. Each entry names what the extra kilobytes buy, so a later reader can judge whether they still buy it.
_trackerNote: 158 → 162 → 165. /tracker carries the exam status panel: the collapsed summary, the expanded stage/date/result detail, and the refresh button with its cooldown timer. Measured at 157.5 kB when the panel landed and 159.9 kB after the menu, which is the same 2.4 kB every other route paid — so 162 → 165 preserves the headroom the 162 was for, rather than granting new room. The panel is a Client Component by requirement: it owns a fetch, a countdown and a disclosure. What it deliberately does NOT ship is the parsing — `status-parse.ts` is server-only, and `report.ts` is imported here for pure accessors with no Zod behind them.
_unmeasuredNote: Routes that emit no prerendered scripts because they are blocking (`export const instant = false`). They are never CDN-served, so first-load JS is not the figure that matters for them. Listing one here is a deliberate act: an unlisted route with no scripts still fails the build, so a route cannot drift out of measurement by accident.
